description: 신규성 점수 8/10: Association Between Weekday-Weekend Sleep Duration Discrepancy (Social Jetlag) and Obesity Risk Among Korean Adolescents: A Nationally Representative Cross-Sectional Study

inputs.title: Association Between Weekday-Weekend Sleep Duration Discrepancy (Social Jetlag) and Obesity Risk Among Korean Adolescents: A Nationally Representative Cross-Sectional Study

outputs.summary: 신규성 점수 8/10: Association Between Weekday-Weekend Sleep Duration Discrepancy (Social Jetlag) and Obesity Risk Among Korean Adolescents: A Nationally Representative Cross-Sectional Study
outputs.gap_identified: No prior study has specifically quantified the association between social jetlag (weekday-weekend sleep midpoint or duration discrepancy) and obesity risk defined by Korean-specific 2017 growth chart percentile cutoffs in a nationally representative sample of Korean adolescents using the 2025 KYRBS dataset.
outputs.suggested_angle: Leverage the large KYRBS sample (n≈60,000) to conduct dose-response analyses of social jetlag severity on obesity risk with stratification by school level (middle vs. high school), sex, and screen time as potential effect modifiers; additionally, incorporate chronotype proxies available in KYRBS to disentangle social jetlag from intrinsic circadian preference, which most prior literature has not done in an East Asian adolescent context.
outputs.llm_justification: The rule-based search returned zero similar papers, and while the broader literature on social jetlag and metabolic outcomes exists (e.g., Roenneberg et al. social jetlag frameworks, Chaput et al. sleep-obesity reviews in youth), none appear to have applied a social jetlag exposure construct to Korean adolescent obesity using the KYRBS and 2017 Korean growth charts, representing a genuine population- and instrument-specific gap. The 2025 KYRBS wave further ensures temporal novelty. A minor downward adjustment from 9 to 8 is warranted because the general conceptual association between irregular sleep schedules and adolescent obesity is well-established in the global literature, meaning the incremental scientific contribution is primarily in population specificity and dataset currency rather than a wholly unprecedented hypothesis.
overall_similar_aspects: Social jetlag as an exposure construct linking weekday-weekend sleep timing discrepancy to health outcomes is established in the sleep epidemiology literature
Cross-sectional design using nationally representative school-based survey data to study adolescent obesity is a common methodological approach
BMI-based obesity classification (percentile cutoffs) as the primary outcome is standard in pediatric obesity research
Adolescent sleep and obesity associations have been examined in multiple prior studies across various national cohorts
Self-reported sleep duration as the basis for exposure ascertainment is widely used and shares measurement limitations with existing studies
overall_different_aspects: Use of the 2025 KYRBS wave — the most recent and previously unpublished cycle — ensures temporal novelty unavailable in any existing published study
Application of Korean-specific 2017 growth chart 95th percentile cutoffs for obesity classification rather than international (WHO/CDC) references tailored to Korean adolescent body composition norms

Nationally representative Korean adolescent population (n≈60,000) with East Asian-specific dietary, academic-stress, and screen-time contexts that modulate sleep architecture differently from Western cohorts

Explicit focus on social jetlag index (midpoint or duration discrepancy) rather than total sleep duration alone as the primary exposure, distinguishing circadian misalignment from mere sleep insufficiency
Potential to examine interaction with Korean-specific academic pressure (hagwon attendance, exam burden) as a structural driver of social jetlag not captured in Western datasets
similar_papers: Social jetlag and obesity among school-aged children: a cross-sectional study (general concept, non-Korean)
Sleep duration and obesity in children and adolescents: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Associations between sleep timing, social jetlag, and cardiometabolic health in adolescents
Physical activity, sedentary behavior, sleep, and obesity in Korean adolescents: findings from the Korea Youth Risk Behavior Web-based Survey (prior KYRBS cycles)

title: [신규성 확인] check_novelty
description: 신규성 점수 6/10: 청소년의 수면 부족과 비만의 연관성

outputs.summary: 신규성 점수 6/10: 청소년의 수면 부족과 비만의 연관성
outputs.gap_identified: While the association between sleep duration and obesity in adolescents is broadly explored globally, no retrieved paper specifically examines this relationship in Korean adolescents using the KYRBS dataset with BMI ≥ 95th percentile as the obesity threshold, leaving a population-specific and dataset-specific evidence gap.
outputs.suggested_angle: To meaningfully differentiate this study, consider incorporating mediating or moderating variables unique to Korean adolescent lifestyle contexts — such as academic stress, screen time, or after-school tutoring (hagwon) attendance — that may confound or modify the sleep-obesity association. Additionally, a trend analysis across multiple KYRBS survey years would add longitudinal ecological depth beyond a single cross-sectional estimate.
outputs.llm_justification: The rule-based similarity score of 8.1/10 reflects that retrieved papers share only the obesity outcome (BMI ≥ 95th percentile in pediatric/adolescent populations) but differ substantially in exposure (sleep duration), population (Korean adolescents), and dataset (KYRBS). Papers such as 'Prevalence of Preclinical and Clinical Obesity Among US Children and Adolescents' (NHANES) and 'Adolescent obesity: Biochemical and dietary disparities in U.S. youth' confirm that analogous work exists in Western populations, which slightly reduces novelty. However, the KYRBS-specific, Korean-context focus with sleep as the primary exposure is not represented in the retrieved literature, justifying a modest downward adjustment to 6/10 given that the sleep-adolescent obesity topic is well-trodden globally and the added value depends heavily on contextual specificity and analytical rigor.
overall_similar_aspects: Outcome variable: obesity defined by BMI percentile cutoff in children/adolescents
Target age group: adolescent or pediatric population
General epidemiological framing of obesity prevalence and correlates
Cross-sectional study design implied by survey-based dataset
overall_different_aspects: Exposure variable: sleep duration as primary independent variable (absent in all retrieved papers)
Population specificity: Korean adolescents with culturally distinct lifestyle patterns (academic pressure, hagwon, screen use)
Dataset: KYRBS (Korea Youth Risk Behavior Survey), not used in any retrieved paper
Potential to capture East Asian-specific BMI-obesity threshold debates and Korean growth reference standards
Policy relevance to Korean public health context and school-based sleep intervention programs

title: [연구 주제 생성] generate_topics
description: 5개 주제 생성: 청소년 비만과 수면

topics.title: Association Between Weekday-Weekend Sleep Duration Discrepancy (Social Jetlag) and Obesity Risk Among Korean Adolescents: A Nationally Representative Cross-Sectional Study
topics.exposure: Social jetlag index derived from sleep_weekday and sleep_weekend (absolute difference in sleep midpoint or duration)
topics.outcome: bmi_category (obesity: 95th percentile or above by 2017 Korean growth charts)
topics.population: Middle and high school students aged 12-18 years participating in the 2025 KYRBS (approximately 60,000 students)
topics.rationale: Social jetlag — the discrepancy between biological and social clocks quantified by weekday-weekend sleep differences — has been linked to metabolic dysregulation in adults, yet evidence in Korean adolescents remains limited. KYRBS 2025 provides both sleep_weekday and sleep_weekend as continuous derived variables, enabling precise social jetlag calculation. Given Korea's high academic burden and documented sleep insufficiency among adolescents, this analysis would address a critical gap and inform school schedule policy. The large nationally representative sample ensures adequate power for sex- and school-level stratified analyses.

topics.title: Prolonged Sedentary Behavior, Inadequate Sleep Duration, and Their Synergistic Association with Overweight and Obesity in Korean Adolescents: Effect Modification by Physical Activity
topics.exposure: Combined sedentary behavior (sit_weekday ≥8 hours) and sleep insufficiency (sleep_weekday <8 hours)
topics.population: All KYRBS 2025 respondents enrolled in middle and high school, analyzed separately by sex and school level
topics.rationale: Sedentary behavior and short sleep duration are independently associated with adolescent obesity, but their joint effect — and whether adequate physical activity modifies this relationship — is insufficiently characterized in Korean youth. KYRBS captures sit_weekday, sit_weekend, sleep_weekday, pa_60min, and pa_vigorous_days, permitting a four-cell exposure matrix (high sedentary × short sleep vs. reference). Identifying synergistic effects would support integrated intervention targeting both screen time reduction and sleep hygiene simultaneously, with high public health relevance given Korea's sedentary academic culture.

topics.title: Mukbang Viewing Frequency, Night Snacking Behavior, and Sleep Quality as a Pathway to Adolescent Obesity: A Mediation Analysis Using 2025 KYRBS Data
topics.exposure: mukbang_watch (frequency of mukbang/cooking show viewing, weekly)
topics.outcome: bmi_category and body_image distortion (discordance between perceived and BMI-classified weight status)
topics.population: Korean middle and high school students in the 2025 KYRBS; subgroup analyses by sex and family economic status
topics.rationale: Mukbang (eating broadcast) viewing is a culturally unique Korean phenomenon newly captured in KYRBS 2025. Mechanistically, mukbang exposure may promote late-night eating (night_snack), disrupt sleep (sleep_weekday, sleep_sufficient), and distort body image (body_image), collectively elevating obesity risk. This study would be among the first nationally representative analyses linking mukbang viewing to adolescent adiposity through behavioral mediators, addressing a novel and policy-relevant question. The 2025 survey's inclusion of zero_drink_intake and sweet_drink_intake further allows dietary covariate adjustment.

topics.title: Socioeconomic Inequalities in the Co-occurrence of Obesity and Sleep Insufficiency Among Korean Adolescents: A Nationally Representative Analysis with Urban-Rural Stratification
topics.exposure: family_econ (subjective economic status, 5-level ordinal) and parental education (father_edu, mother_edu)
topics.outcome: Dual burden: concurrent bmi_category ≥85th percentile AND sleep_weekday <8 hours (composite binary outcome)
topics.population: KYRBS 2025 participants stratified by region (대도시, 중소도시, 군지역) and school level; multicultural adolescents (parent_nationality) examined as a vulnerable subgroup
topics.rationale: Health inequalities in Korean adolescents are understudied, particularly for co-occurring obesity and sleep deprivation — a phenotype associated with worse cardiometabolic outcomes than either condition alone. KYRBS enables linkage of family_econ, parental education, region, and residence_type with both BMI and sleep outcomes across a nationally representative sample. Urban-rural disparities and multicultural minority status add equity dimensions with direct policy implications for targeted public health interventions. The complex survey design ensures valid national estimates across all socioeconomic strata.

topics.title: Sleep Duration, Subjective Sleep Sufficiency, and Weight Control Behaviors in Korean Adolescents: Examining the Role of Body Image Distortion as a Mediator
topics.exposure: sleep_weekday (continuous, hours) and sleep_sufficient (subjective sleep quality, 3-level)
topics.outcome: weight_control (weight loss attempt behavior) and unhealthy weight control practices (inferred from weight_control combined with bmi_category discordance)
topics.population: KYRBS 2025 respondents with available BMI, body_image, sleep, and weight_control data; sex-disaggregated analyses prioritized given known sex differences in body image
topics.rationale: Short sleep duration elevates appetite-regulating hormones and promotes weight gain, yet simultaneously may trigger compensatory — often unhealthy — weight control behaviors in body-conscious adolescents. Body image distortion (discordance between actual BMI category and subjective body_image perception) may mediate this pathway. KYRBS provides all necessary variables: sleep_weekday, sleep_sufficient, bmi_category, body_image, and weight_control. This study addresses an underexplored bidirectional relationship between sleep and weight management behaviors, with implications for both obesity prevention and eating disorder risk reduction programs in Korean schools.
